description:
src/lib.rs:24      pub use jmap_base_client::ClientError;
src/methods/mod.rs:28-31  pub use jmap_types::{AddedItem, ChangesResponse, GetResponse,
                            QueryChangesResponse, QueryResponse, SetError, SetResponse};

Every public method on SessionClient returns Result<..., jmap_base_client::ClientError>. Every /get and /set method returns a jmap_types::* type re-exported through this crate.

Contract consequence: once this crate ships to crates.io, jmap-mail-client 0.x.y's public surface is permanently tied to jmap-types and jmap-base-client major-version compatibility. If either crate cuts a 0.2.0 with a breaking change to ClientError or GetResponse, jmap-mail-client's API breaks transitively. Consumers cannot pin jmap-mail-client = "0.1" and stay buildable without also pinning compatible versions of the two upstream crates.

The same applies to the seven extension-client siblings via canonical-template propagation.

Today path = "../crate-jmap-*" deps mask this — it cannot bite until publish. But the publishing handshake will be brittle: a coordinated bump of all 30 crates becomes mandatory, with no incremental escape.

Three contract documentation gaps:

  1. The crate's README and rustdoc do not warn callers that the error type and response types are re-exports.
  2. The Cargo.toml does not document the version-pinning relationship.
  3. There is no "stability story" docstring on the crate root explaining the re-export pattern.

Recommendation:

  (a) Document the re-export pattern explicitly in the crate-root docstring and Gotchas section, naming the upstream crates whose major versions are locked.

  (b) When publishing, declare jmap-mail-client = "0.1" alongside the precise jmap-types and jmap-base-client versions it was built against, and document the pinning relationship in the Cargo.toml description or a per-crate stability comment.

  (c) Consider whether GetResponse/SetResponse/ChangesResponse/QueryResponse should be re-exported from jmap-types or NEWTYPED in this crate (which would break callers but isolate the major-version surface). For 0.x.y a wrapping newtype is plausible; for 1.0 it is essentially mandatory. File a follow-up bead for the 1.0 stability cut deciding this.

Note: this finding is a category-rather-than-line issue. It does not block any specific feature; it informs the 1.0 cut. Not high priority but important enough to capture.
title: Public re-exports of jmap-types and jmap-base-client items lock major-version compatibility
